2. How a route is registered (Composio's documented steps, as done here)

POST https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/custom/toolkits/upsert with the body in section 3. Composio adds the CUSTOM_ prefix. app_url and auth_schemes can't change later: a change returns 409, so delete the toolkit and register it again.
2. Create its auth config (API key and OAuth routes only)

POST https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/auth_configs with {"toolkit": {"slug": "CUSTOM_<SLUG>"}, "auth_config": {"type": "use_custom_auth", "authScheme": "API_KEY", "credentials": {}, "is_enabled_for_tool_router": true}}. Without the tool-router flag, calls fail with NoActiveConnection.
GET /api/v3/auth_configs lists it ENABLED with is_enabled_for_tool_router true (all 13 of ours are).

python3 ~/.agents/tools/connectors/push_key_to_composio.py --item "<1Password item>" --toolkit custom_<slug>. It reads the key with the read-write robot and creates an ACTIVE API_KEY login with generic_api_key. Composio doesn't test the key. For the GHL builder (OAuth), connect through Composio's sign-in link instead.

The first sync starts by itself when the first login becomes ACTIVE (at registration for no-auth readers). After the server's tools change: POST /api/v3.1/custom/toolkits/sync with {"slug": "CUSTOM_<SLUG>", "connected_account_id": "<ca_...>"} (no account id for a no-auth reader).
The reply gives a version and synced_count.

5. Header names for the two upstream API-key routes (G12 addendum, spp-c13)
Authorization: Bearer <Cloudflare API token>. User and account tokens both work; account tokens need Account Resources : Read; tokens with Client IP Address Filtering are not supported.
API_KEY with one field, generic_api_key. Composio's API doesn't return the header template the toolkit was registered with.
Authorization: <Foreplay API key>, with no Bearer prefix.

6. Finding the For You project ID (x-project-id) on a new org, and every place to change it (G12 addendum, spp-c13 and spp-c14)
Which project holds the connector logins?
The For You project (here pr_JDtrNq9tUa_i). Platform and For You are separate dashboard surfaces.

The For You dashboard's Settings page shows only the org name, Enhanced Control and Delete organization. composio whoami and composio orgs list show no project. GET /api/v3/org/project/list and GET /api/v3/auth/session/info return only the Platform project (here alex_workspace_first_project).

POST https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/org/consumer/project/resolve with x-user-api-key and x-org-id returns project_nano_id, the value to send as x-project-id. It provisions the consumer project if it's missing, so it's a new org's first step; it wasn't called on our org. The documented read-only listing (GET /api/v3.1/org/consumer/connected_toolkits?user_id=…) returned no project fields on our org (live, 2026-10-01).
Where is it on an existing org (read-only)?

In the composio CLI's own cache, after composio login and one composio execute: the entry in ~/.composio/tool-permissions-cache.json whose key contains :consumer- holds orgId, projectId and consumerUserId. Print them with: python3 -c 'import json,os;d=json.load(open(os.path.expanduser("~/.composio/tool-permissions-cache.json")));[print(v["orgId"],v["projectId"],v["consumerUserId"]) for k,v in d["entries"].items() if ":consumer-" in k]'

Nothing in the Mac scripts: push_key_to_composio.py, ir_notes/sync_notes.py and the tune-up's tuneup.py find the project themselves through composio_project.py (--project, then COMPOSIO_PROJECT_ID, then the composio CLI cache) and stop with a message when none is set; a new org sets COMPOSIO_PROJECT_ID. The hub's health check reads composio_project from health/config.json, so put the same ID there (Rebuild from zero, section 10a). The composio card's REST line is text only, queued for the card rebuild.
7. The GHL builder's DCR auth config (G12 addendum, spp-c13)
DCR_OAUTH, not Composio-managed. Scopes: mcp:read, mcp:write, offline_access. oauth_redirect_uri: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add
